title: O Saviour, Cast a Gracious Smile
description: O Saviour, Cast a Gracious Smile in Tonic Solfa to HOLY MATRIMONY, doh is G: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 5 verses and a piano.
about: Charles Wesley wrote these words. His brother John printed them in A Collection of Hymns for the Use of the People Called Methodists (1780), hymn 528.
The book printed the words without tunes. They are in Common Particular Metre (8.8.6.8.8.6), and this page sets them to HOLY MATRIMONY; any other Common Particular Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: O Sa-viour, cast a gra-cious smile! Our gloo-my guilt, and self-ish guile, And shy dis-trust re-move; The true sim-plic-i-ty im-part, To fash-ion ev-ery pas-sive heart, And mould it in-to love.

lines: O Saviour, cast a gracious smile!
Our gloomy guilt, and selfish guile,
Our naked hearts to thee we raise;
Whate'er obstructs thy work of grace,
Soon as in thee we gain a part,
Our spirit purged from nature's art
We then pursue our sole design,
To lose our melting will in thine,
O that we now the power might feel
To do on earth thy blessed will,
In thee, the Life, the Truth, the Way,
To walk, and perfectly to obey
And spread the spark of living fire
And give us now to find in thee

source: John Wesley, A Collection of Hymns for the Use of the People Called Methodists (1780)
licence: Public domain: Charles Wesley died in 1788.
credits: Words by Charles Wesley (1707–1788), public domain, as printed in John Wesley's Collection of Hymns (1780); set to HOLY MATRIMONY by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
